subject: Re: FinTechCo - API auth & key management follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinTechCo - API authn & key management

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration and the auth story. Nice to meet you and the security team.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: server-side integration to call Redwood endpoints for generation, embeddings, and a reranker.
- Traffic profile: batch embedding jobs + bursty real-time generation (predictable 200 reqs/min, spikes to 1k).
- Data sensitivity: PII in a small subset; customer data residency in US-only.

Auth/options you mentioned we should validate:
1) API keys (server-side) + key rotation cadence
2) Service accounts + JWT/OAuth server-to-server flow (preferred for scoped access)
3) KMS integration (customer-managed keys with envelope encryption)

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm which of the above you currently support (API keys vs service accounts vs OAuth)?
- What is your key rotation policy today (automated rotation every X days?)
- Are there any firewall/VPC allowlist requirements for outgoing calls to Redwood?
- Would you be open to a short technical sync (30m) next week to walk engineers through a sample service-account flow?

I've attached our short "auth patterns" one-pager that maps Redwood's integrations to each option.

Attachment: redwood-auth-patterns.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinTechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - API authn & key management

Hi Marissa —

Great to meet you as well. Short answers inline:

- What we support: we currently use service accounts for server-to-server flows (internal microservices). We also have API keys for legacy partners but prefer moving new integrations to service accounts + JWT/OAuth for scoped access.
- Rotation policy: service account keys are rotated every 90 days. We have an internal job that creates new key material and bumps the active key.
- KMS: Yes — we store private keys in our HSM-backed KMS (CloudKMS).
- Firewall: outbound to Redwood's API domain is allowed; we can restrict to IP ranges if needed.

We can do the 30m tech sync. Availability next week: Tue/Thu mornings PST.

Attachment: FinTechCo-service-account-details.vcf (contact card)

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Engineering Manager — Platform
Alex Johnson
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Thanks Alex — this is helpful. Looping in Neha (our security lead) to confirm compatibility and call out any gap items on our side.

Proposed integration approach (short):
1) Service-account JWT flow (recommended):
   - FinTechCo creates a service account and stores private key in your KMS.
   - At runtime, your services mint a short-lived JWT signed with that key and exchange for a Redwood access token via our token-exchange endpoint.
   - Token TTLs can be short (minutes) to minimize blast radius; we support rotation and token revocation.
2) API key fallback for quick POC:
   - We issue a scoped API key restricted to embedding/generation endpoints for initial testing; keys should be stored server-side and rotated.

Open questions for the sync:
- Do you want us to support direct KMS integration (customer-managed key for payload envelope encryption)?
- Any compliance requirements for token retention / audit logs we should surface?

Suggested next steps:
- 30m tech sync: Tue 2027-06-29 09:00 PST (proposed Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210)
- I will bring a short runbook and sample policy. Attached is our example service-account policy yaml you can share with your infra team.

Attachment: example-service-account-policy.yaml

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - API authn & key management

Folks — quick note from security: we support the JWT service-account flow outlined by Marissa. A few implementation notes from our side:

- Redwood supports token exchange and short-lived access tokens (configurable TTL; we recommend <= 15 minutes for high-sensitivity workloads).
- We can support customer-managed keys for envelope encryption; we'll need a short onboarding checklist for KMS access and audit logging configuration.
- Rotation: we recommend a rolling key rotation where the old key remains valid for a grace period (7 days) to avoid downtime; our token revocation API can be called if a key is compromised.

Next steps:
- Confirm Tue 2027-06-29 09:00 PST for the technical sync.
- Alex: if you can share a short list of IPs that need allowlisting (or confirm you prefer DNS), we'll have our infra ready.
- I'll share the onboarding checklist and a short runbook after the call.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
